newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria liberalises domestic fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria liberalises domestic fuel prices.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Tuesday agreed to liberalise domestic prices for petrol and diesel but said import taxes and customs duties would remain in force.
"In line with pledges made to international financial institutions, retail prices are not expected to change," interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski told reporters.
"Liberalisation means that the government will no longer set maximum prices for fuels, but suppliers and importers will set prices according to costs."
Sofianski said customs duties of 25 percent and import tax of five percent would remain in force so that the indebted state refinery Neftochim would not face unfair competition.
The decision becomes effective on publication in the State Gazette. The next issue is on Friday.

Since April 1, petrol prices have ranged between 910-1140 levs per litre depending on the grade, while diesel costs 630 levs/litre. The government calculated the prices at a rate of 1,692 levs per dollar, and the lev traded near 1,500 to the dollar on Tuesday.
Petrol retailers said they did not expect an immediate shakeup of the market.

"We do not expect a change of prices at the beginning, either a rise or a drop," said Kamelia Slaveikova, spokeswoman for Shell Bulgaria, a Royal Dutch/Shell Group subsidiary and the only foreign fuel retailer in Bulgaria.
Bulgarian private retailer Litex said fuel prices had been low and retailers had been making a loss from selling petrol and making a profit only from their shops at petrol stations.
"Fuel prices are low enough and I do not expect them to be reduced by any other firm," Litex publicity director Rozimir Rozev told Reuters.
